item: The shutdown writes the -wal back before it disposes the pool, and the previous-session text says when it was left
status: built (draft PR; the 17 Oct local bundle rebased onto main f3e67b0a3)
refs: PR #1475; coordinator 17 Oct 11:21: diff list approved as a local bundle, re-gated on main after #1429 and #1435 merged, D1 no time cap, D2 a straggler inside a read leaves the log and records it, the text must say the log was left
summary: The 10-10 session ended clean and left a 1.41 GB -wal (90.8 s of the next unlock). Engine.dispose() closes only the pool's idle connections and SQLite writes the log back when the LAST connection closes, so one connection still checked out leaves 100 % of it (measured: 300 MiB, plain and encrypted, straggler idle or inside a read). The lifespan now runs one no-wait PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) from a connection of its own (busy_timeout 0 first; empties the log with an idle straggler in 2.2 s for 300 MiB, returns busy at once and leaves it with a straggler inside a read), between the storage guard's stop and the disposal. dispose_engine() returns the pool's own checked-out count (None plus a reason when the pool has none). The sentinel's dispose-done phase carries wal_bytes_after_dispose, connections_checked_out_at_dispose and shutdown_checkpoint, shutdown_began_at is stamped once on the first phase, and the Previous session text prints 'the -wal was LEFT by that session's end: N bytes' (and the teardown's duration) whatever the verdict: clean stays 'the teardown ran'. Deviation from the diff list: the unlock path's _close_after_checkpoint is untouched (a separate helper, because 5 tests and a sink-sweep pin name that function and #1429 edits its file). Not changed: src/safety/shutdown.py's early dispose before SIGTERM (the lifespan step that follows covers it). A kill in the middle of the step reads as an unclean end during shutdown, which is true. tests/test_shutdown_wal.py: 20 tests, plain and encrypted; two mutants (PASSIVE for TRUNCATE; no zero busy timeout) are red.
